script.title: I copied the list. Why did both change?

dialogue.speaker: motu
dialogue.text: I copied my to-do list, removed a task from the copy, and the original lost it too! Why?

dialogue.speaker: patlu
dialogue.text: Because you never copied it. backup equals tasks just gives the same list a second name, so both names point to one list.

broll.code:
tasks = ['buy milk', 'study']
backup = tasks
backup.remove('study')
print(tasks)  # ['buy milk']

dialogue.speaker: patlu

dialogue.speaker: motu
dialogue.text: Wait. What if every task is a dictionary, and I change a title in the copy? What happens to the original?

pause.prompt: You copy a list of dictionaries with .copy() and change one task's title in the copy. What happens to the original?

dialogue.speaker: patlu
dialogue.text: The original changes too. copy is shallow: a new list, but the same dictionaries inside. For nested data, use copy dot deepcopy.

script.takeaway: Assigning a list gives it a second name; use .copy() for a new list, and copy.deepcopy when the items are nested.

dialogue.speaker: jack
dialogue.text: Let's rank the ways to center a card on a portfolio page. One rule: centered horizontally and vertically, on any screen size.

dialogue.speaker: jack

dialogue.speaker: jack

dialogue.speaker: jack

dialogue.speaker: jack

pause.prompt: position: absolute + top/left 50% + translate(-50%, -50%). Where does it rank for centering a card?

dialogue.speaker: jack

dialogue.speaker: jack
dialogue.text: Flexbox with justify-content and align-items center. Same result, works everywhere. Also S.

script.takeaway: Use flexbox or grid on the parent to center both ways; margin auto only centers horizontally.

script.title: Stop the useEffect request loop

pr.title: Fix order polling loop in useOrders

dialogue.speaker: jhatka
dialogue.text: This line was the bug. A new query object is built on every render, so the effect sees a changed dependency every single time.

pr.display: new object every render = effect every render 💀

dialogue.speaker: jhatka
dialogue.text: And the effect calls setOrders, which renders again, which builds a new object again. That loop hammered the orders API.

pr.display: setOrders → rerender → new object → effect again 🔁

dialogue.speaker: john
dialogue.text: The fix wraps the object in useMemo. Quick check: when does it actually build a new object now?

pr.display: useMemo now. when does it rebuild? 🤔

pause.prompt: useMemo(() => ({ ...filters, page: 1 }), [filters.status, filters.from]). When does it build a new object?
choices: Only when status or from change

dialogue.speaker: john
dialogue.text: Only when status or from change. Those are plain strings, compared by value, so the effect runs once per real filter change.

pr.display: deps are strings → compared by value ✅ one fetch per real change

dialogue.speaker: jhatka
dialogue.text: One follow-up: if someone adds a new filter field later, it must join this dependency list too, or the orders go stale.

pr.display: nit: new filter fields must join these deps or data goes stale 👀

dialogue.speaker: jhatka
dialogue.text: Approving. Lesson: effect dependencies should be values, not objects you rebuild on every render.

pr.display: LGTM 🚀 deps = values, not fresh objects

script.takeaway: Effect dependencies should be values, not objects rebuilt on every render.

script.title: Why memory kept climbing

dialogue.speaker: john
dialogue.text: Our Go price service used more memory every hour, until it got restarted. Here's the request path.

dialogue.speaker: john
dialogue.text: The handler starts a goroutine to fetch a price, then waits on a channel for the result.

dialogue.speaker: john
dialogue.text: It also has a two second timeout, so one slow API can't hang the whole request.

dialogue.speaker: john
dialogue.text: Now the API takes five seconds. The handler times out and returns. What happens to that goroutine?

pause.prompt: The handler has returned. The goroutine later sends on an unbuffered channel that nobody reads. What happens?

dialogue.speaker: john
dialogue.text: It blocks forever. Nobody receives on that unbuffered channel anymore, so every slow request leaves one stuck goroutine behind.

dialogue.speaker: john
dialogue.text: The fix: give the channel a buffer of one, so the send never blocks, and pass a context so the fetch stops early.

script.takeaway: A goroutine sending on an unbuffered channel nobody reads blocks forever; buffer the channel and pass a context.

questions.prompt: Why did each slow request leak a goroutine?
choices: Its send on an unbuffered channel blocked forever after the handler left
questions.explanation: An unbuffered send waits for a receiver; once the handler returned, no receiver remained.

learning.takeaway: A goroutine sending on an unbuffered channel nobody reads blocks forever; buffer the channel and pass a context.

script.title: OOMKilled ke fixes, ranked

dialogue.speaker: budhdev
dialogue.text: Hamari Node API Kubernetes par baar baar OOMKilled ho rahi thi. Criterion ek hi: crash band ho, aur memory bhi barbaad na ho.

dialogue.speaker: budhdev
dialogue.text: Limit hi hata do? Pod node ki saari memory kha sakta hai aur baaki pods ko bhi gira dega. Seedha F.

dialogue.speaker: budhdev
dialogue.text: Har raat pods restart karo. Crash thoda kam dikhega, par leak wahin ka wahin. D tier.

dialogue.speaker: budhdev
dialogue.text: Memory limit badha do. Abhi ke liye theek, par leak hai toh bas thodi der se crash hoga. C tier.

dialogue.speaker: budhdev
dialogue.text: Ab Node ka max old space size, container ki limit se thoda kam. Yeh kitna kaam ka hai?

pause.prompt: Node's --max-old-space-size is set a bit below the container's memory limit. What does that change?
choices: Node collects garbage harder before the kernel kills the pod

dialogue.speaker: budhdev
dialogue.text: Node limit ke paas pahunchne se pehle hi zor se garbage collection karta hai, kernel ke maarne se pehle. A tier.

dialogue.speaker: budhdev
dialogue.text: Aur leak dhoondh ke code theek karna, jaise kabhi na saaf hone wala cache. Asli ilaaj yahi hai. S tier.

script.takeaway: Find the leak; until then, keep Node's heap limit below the container limit so it collects garbage before the kernel kills it.

questions.prompt: Why is removing the memory limit F tier?
choices: One leaking pod can eat the node's memory and take other pods down
questions.explanation: Without a limit the leak grows until the whole node runs out of memory.

script.title: Why won't Rust let me push here?

dialogue.speaker: oggy
dialogue.text: Rust won't compile my log parser. I push to a vector while looping over it, and it says cannot borrow as mutable. Why so strict?

dialogue.speaker: jack
dialogue.text: Because pushing can move the vector to new memory, while your loop still holds a reference into the old memory. Rust stops it at compile time.

dialogue.speaker: oggy
dialogue.text: So in C, this would just crash at runtime instead?

dialogue.speaker: jack
dialogue.text: Or quietly read freed memory, which is worse. Rust turns that bug into a compiler error.

dialogue.speaker: oggy
dialogue.text: Fine, but I still need the error lines. What's the clean way to collect them?

pause.prompt: You need the ERROR lines without changing the vector you're iterating over. What's the idiomatic fix?
choices: Collect them into a new vector with filter
Clone the vector on every iteration

dialogue.speaker: jack
dialogue.text: Build a new vector instead of growing the one you're reading. One iterator chain, and no fight with the borrow checker.

script.takeaway: Don't grow a vector while iterating over it; build a new one with an iterator chain instead.

choices: A push can reallocate the vector while the loop still references it
questions.explanation: Reallocation would leave the loop's reference pointing at freed memory.

dialogue.speaker: jhatka
dialogue.text: Purane code mein get aur set alag alag the. Do requests ek saath aayi, toh dono ne same count padha.

pause.prompt: Two requests call INCR on the same key at the same moment. What do they get back?

dialogue.speaker: paplu

dialogue.speaker: jhatka
dialogue.text: Ek baat: agar incr ke baad aur expire se pehle server crash ho gaya, toh key kabhi expire nahi hogi. Isse ek Lua script mein daal do.

dialogue.speaker: jhatka
dialogue.text: Approve, follow up ke saath. Counter ke kaam mein hamesha atomic operation use karo.
